moat_against: Merchant/competitive generation and LatAm assets carry commodity, FX and political risk; chronic asset impairments ($1,079M in 2023, $337M in 2025 per the 10-K cash-flow statement)
Gross margin compressed from 27.9% (2020) to 18.1% (2025) in fundamentals.json — no demonstrated pricing power
Growth is bought with capex that has exceeded operating cash flow every year since 2022, funded by ~$29B of debt and tax-equity/NCI capital
Regulators cap returns at the US utilities and FERC now decides whether the take-private itself proceeds
moat_for: Regulated US utility franchises (AES Ohio, AES Indiana) — local monopolies with rate-base recovery
Long-term contracted PPAs: 10.9 GW contracted backlog at Q2 2026, 3.8 GW under construction
Scale global power platform (32+ GW) with data-center demand pull — Indiana approval to power a Google data center (Oct 2026)
moat_justification: Regulated utility franchises and a 10.9 GW contracted PPA backlog give contracted, visible cash flows, but the moat is capped at 4: gross margin fell from 27.9% (2020) to 18.1% (2025), returns are regulator-capped where they are safe and commodity/FX-exposed where they are not, and growth capex has consumed more than operating cash flow for four straight years, leaving owner's earnings negative in 0 of the last 5 years. The engine could not compute an ROIC proxy (operating income and debt tags blank in EDGAR), so no ROIC-above-cost-of-capital evidence supports a higher score.
name: THE AES CORPORATION
one_liner: Contracted power platform with a weak 4/10 moat and no positive owner's earnings in 5 years (growth capex exceeds OCF) — Tier F on the OE model; the stock is a merger-arb stub anyway, pinned at $14.95 against the GIP/EQT $15.00 cash take-private expected to close late 2026/early 2027.
